title: Multi-tenant Prefix Bloom Index and Lazy Merge for GPU KV Sharing
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Introduce a lightweight multi-tenant prefix membership index (Bloom-based) and a lazy merge workflow to enable high-confidence cross-request prefix deduplication without expensive eager KV consolidation. Goal: increase effective KV cache reuse across sessions and tenants while reducing GPU slab fragmentation and peak memory pressure for continuous-batching workloads.
rationale: Existing prefix dedupe relies on exact fingerprint registries and heavy centralized merges that require copying or pinning large KV fragments on the GPU, which increases memory pressure and latency during peak batching. A probabilistic pre-filter (Bloom index) reduces false positive work and lets us do low-cost checks in CPU memory before attempting GPU-resident operations. Coupled with a lazy merge and reference-counted shadow mapping, we can avoid immediate slab relocations and amortize consolidation work during low-load periods.
proposal: 1) Maintain a per-shard, per-tenant Bloom membership index stored off-GPU (CPU memory) that summarizes prefix fingerprints currently present in the GPU KV slabs. 2) On request arrival, consult Bloom index to short-circuit miss paths; only when Bloom indicates presence do we probe the fast metadata layer to obtain a stable pointer. 3) Implement a lazy merge coordinator that performs background consolidation of colocated fragments: it creates ephemeral merged views (virtual mappings) for hot prefixes while scheduling physical compaction during background windows. 4) Add a small shadow-refcount map (compact 32-bit counters) that tracks soft references from virtual views; evictions consider both physical refs and shadow refs. 5) Integrate with continuous-batching by exposing a minor API handshake for the batcher to optionally prefer virtual mappings when assembling KV for tokens to avoid copying.
design_decisions: Use counting Bloom filter (two 16-bit counters per bucket) to allow low-cost deletes versus a plain Bloom to support eviction updates.
Keep full fingerprint->fragment pointer metadata in a compact CPU-side index; only hot pointers are mirrored to GPU metadata to reduce resident metadata size.
Lazy merge will create immutable virtual mappings that reference original fragment slices; physical compaction will be scheduled by LRU-weighted background workers to minimize tail latency impact.
Eviction policy will combine a slab-packing score and shadow-reference penalty to avoid reclaiming fragments still referenced by virtual views used in in-flight batches.
Rollout via canary on a dedicated cluster with synthetic workload first, then a limited percentage of production requests for non-critical tenants.
Design keeps cryptographic integrity of fingerprints; no customer data is stored in Bloom filters (only hashed fingerprints).
milestones: 2026-03-05: Prototype counting-Bloom and CPU metadata store (done)
2026-03-12: Integration with batcher path and virtual mapping API (in review)
2026-03-28: Canary rollout on dedicated-dev cluster + perf validation (planned)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end validation shows >= 18% increase in cross-request KV reuse hit rate on our CV workload mix compared to baseline
Peak GPU memory usage (p99.9 across runs) reduced by >= 12% on benchmark traces that previously suffered fragmentation
No more than 3% regression in P95 tail latency for generation requests during steady-state traffic
Background compaction tasks must not push GPU memory above burst threshold; compaction must be throttled automatically during high load
Feature gated and staged: must support a runtime flag per-tenant and be able to roll back without data corruption
tasks: Implement counting-Bloom library with efficient vectorized insert/test/remove
Build compact CPU metadata index for fingerprint->fragment-slice mapping
Expose virtual mapping API for the runtime batch assembler
Add shadow-refcount map and extend eviction decision logic
Implement background compaction worker with throttling and scheduling heuristics
Add telemetry: bloom false-positive rate, virtual-mapping usage, compaction time, shadow-ref counts
Add unit/integration tests and end-to-end perf harness scenario
Create migration/rollback docs and feature flags for canary rollout
risks: Bloom false positives could cause additional GPU probes; need tuned parameters to keep work amplification acceptable
Shadow refcounts introduce bookkeeping overhead; poor implementation could negate memory gains
Background compaction could interfere with peak workloads if throttling fails
Cross-tenant index semantics require careful isolation to avoid bleed-through; must validate privacy assumptions
Rollback path complexity if virtual mappings are materialized into long-lived refs
tests: Unit: counting-Bloom correctness (insert/test/remove) with randomized inputs
Integration: CPU metadata <-> GPU pointer reconciliation under concurrent inserts/evictions
Perf: replay of 7-day production prefix arrival trace comparing baseline vs feature on tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory usage
Chaos: force eviction races and worker restarts to ensure refcount invariants and safe rollback
A/B: controlled percentage of traffic for canary tenants with metrics dashboard and automatic rollback threshold
